Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how customers open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

According to recent reports, opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

Recent findings suggest that you can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point consumers toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Industry observers note that apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

Sources indicate that the last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Industry observers note that now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

According to recent reports, apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

Sources indicate that after 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s upcoming Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the upcoming behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

In a recent development, iOS 27 brought several new features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.

With iOS 27, Apple fixed a lot of bugs and also granted many feature requests from over the years.

Siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a major upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar, Mail, and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.

In Messages, there’s a newly introduced setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.

Sources indicate that the audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.

Since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of users have encountered—including Justin Bieber—it’s very easy to hit by accident.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:.

Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’.

If you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.

In a recent development, will you disable the audio button in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-latest iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

In a recent development, the iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

In a recent development, the iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

Recent findings suggest that the iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

In a recent development, for most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON: If extreme weather doesn’t shutter theaters in the Northeast, then Lionsgate is looking forward to a lucrative Thanksgiving stretch with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping potentially banking $85M+ over five-days.

Industry observers note that should the sixth title in the Suzanne Collins series file in that range, it will rep the second best Thanksgiving haul for a Hunger Games movie after Catching Fire‘s $109.9M Wednesday-Sunday turkey take 13 years ago. Sunrise on the Reaping‘s Wednesday is looking like $15.5M-$16.5M with a second 3-day weekend around $58M-$65M at 4,018 theaters, -46% to -51%. Five day forecasts are always a challenge for the industry to predict: Business dips on Thanksgiving then spikes on Black Friday, which is one of the most active moviegoing days of the year. By Sunday, we’re looking at a running cume for the Francis Lawrence directed movie of $233M domestic, which would be 40% higher than the lifetime cume on 2023’s Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.

Second will either be Disney’s Hexed at 3,725 theaters or Universal/Paramount’s Focker-in-Law at 3,382 sites. Hexed is seeing around $7.8M today (including $2.1M previews), for a 3-day around $20M and 5-day between $35M-$40M. Let’s see if this picks up before passing complete judgement on this $200M original animation production, but it’s clear Hexed isn’t Coco or Frozen. Watch on Deadline.

Focker-in-Law is seeing a $5.2M Wednesday, 3-day of $24.8M and 5-day of $36.1M. No Rotten Tomatoes audience scores yet on either title.

Fourth goes to Paramount’s third frame of Johnny Depp Christmas movie, Ebenezer with $1.5M today at 3,180 sites and a 3-day between $6.8M-$7.3M, -6% to -13%, for a 5-day of $10M-$10.6M and running cume on the high end of $45.9M.

Fifth is Amazon MGM Studio’s fourth frame of I Play Rocky at 2,711 with $1.4M today, 3-day of $6.6M, and 5-day of $9.5M for a running cume of $22.5M.

Outside the top 5 is Netflix’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at 251 locations with $1M today, $3M 3-day and 5-day of $5M.

WEDNESDAY AM: As we told you last night, Lionsgate scored its best Tuesday ever at the domestic box office with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and the best ever for the Suzanne Collins franchise as the day raked in $15.98M.

It has been revealed that 2013’s The Hunger Games: Catching Fire owned the previous best Tuesday for the franchise with $15.96M. Running cume for the fifth Francis Lawrence movie is $148.1M and by Thanksgiving, Sunrise on the Reaping will surpass its previous 2023 chapter’s lifetime domestic B.O. of $166.3M.

As we told you, Sunrise on the Reaping will dominate the Thanksgiving Wednesday through Sunday stretch as the franchise has historically done before since 2013, this time with a floor of $70M+. Previously, the pics over Thanksgiving cooked up the following: Catching Fire ($109.9M), Mockingjay Part 1 ($82.6M), Mockingjay Part 2 ($75.9M) with Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes way behind ($42.2M).

Lionsgate has had back-to-back global hit openings this year with Sunrise on the Reaping last weekend at $226.1M WW and Michael with $218.8M. This has all happened under the administration and watch of Motion Picture Chairman, Adam Fogelson. Still no word out there whether or not Lionsgate rejected or accepted Legendary’s bid.

Industry observers note that walt Disney Animation’s Hexed came in with $2.1M, $100K above the $2M we were spotting yesterday. That preview figure is higher than Encanto ($1.5M previews, 5-day of $40.5M) and Wish ($1.8M previews including $500K Saturday sneaks; 5-day of $31.6M). No RT audience score yet, but critics were meh at 67% fresh. There is a chance that the traditional Disney pic comes in lower than its 5-day forecast of $40M-$45M as original animated titles are very challenging to launch in the streaming era, but you have to start some place.

Recent findings suggest that universal and Paramount’s Focker-in-Law, which didn’t have previews last night, rather began showtimes at midnight, has more potential to hit its 5-day forecast of $45M given the Ariana Grande factor and the fact that audiences love the franchise. The first Meet the Parents 26 years ago was the fave among critics at 85% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes. Focker-in-Law isn’t the worst at 26%, as that belongs to 2010’s Little Fockers. 2004’s Meet the Fockers stands at 39%.

Hexed, Focker-in-Law and Sunrise on the Reaping are sharing PLFs with the latter having Imax screens (except for AMC where they are being designated to Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth).

Thank God for Lionsgate Hunger Games at the box office: Sans a Wicked, Moana and a Zootopia, the Thanksgiving box office will certainly be down from last year’s five day robust $290.3M, which was the fifth best ever. Moana 2 and Wicked led the holiday to its best haul ever with $424.9M.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I write a lot about e-readers and e-ink tablets for Lifehacker, and one matter I'm constantly grappling with is how to write informatively about a bunch of devices that can be quite different in some details, like build or native firmware, and pretty much identical in others, given that literally all e-ink devices use display technology produced by the same Chinese company. (It's called E-Ink.) The best way to do this is to include more video in my articles, but I've lacked a good way to film hands-free so I can easily demonstrate a device's look and feel—until recently.

I recently got an offer to try out a magnetic neck mount from Telesin, a low-cost option to turn my iPhone into a wearable so I can keep my hands free while filming. It's a pretty basic concept, but well-executed: The band that goes around your neck is made of rubber with a firm but flexible core, so you can easily position it to be longer or shorter or at an angle, and the phone mount is on an extending arm with three joints to give you additional options.

According to recent reports, I haven't had a chance to film anything for public consumption quite yet, but my testing has already given me some great ideas for how I can use it to show off, say, what it's really like to use a micro-reader in comparison to a full-sized Kindle, as I'll be able to wear it to give a more accurate user's point of view. And right now is a good time to pick one of them up, as many of Telesin's phone and camera accessories (including similar models built to handle an action camera like a GoPro) are discounted for Black Friday; the one I tested is down to $17, or 15% off.

This won't be the right device for every filming scenario. Though MagSafe holds my iPhone fairly securely, I found that I would accidentally detach it every time I tried to adjust the shooting angle—once even leading me to drop it. That's potentially bad news, as using it may require you to take the phone out of its case if it isn't MagSafe-compatible. (Mine isn't.) But if you're just looking for an inexpensive way to shoot hands-free video in a controlled environment, it could be exactly what you need.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Sources indicate that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Recent findings suggest that the best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Industry observers note that say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

It has been revealed that A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Upcoming York Mayor Zohran Mamdani struck a personal note during a press briefing Wednesday about the postponement of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade due to a major storm.
  • According to recent reports, “Many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow,” the mayor mentioned.
  • Organizers and city officials, made the call earlier Wednesday to push the 100th annual edition of the parade to Saturday morning, when the forecast calls for sunny skies and temperatures in the 40s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upcoming York Mayor Zohran Mamdani struck a personal note during a press briefing Wednesday about the postponement of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade due to a major storm.

According to recent reports, “Many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow,” the mayor mentioned. “I know that this change of aims will cause inconveniences. Yet safety has to come first. On Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker, and everyone visiting, will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe.”.

Organizers and city officials, made the call earlier Wednesday to push the 100th annual edition of the parade to Saturday morning, when the forecast calls for sunny skies and temperatures in the 40s. A Nor’easter, a classic storm pattern, is expected to bring drenching rain and high winds to New York and many other parts of the Northeast on Thursday and into Friday. Forecasters are calling for as much as 2 inches of rain in New York, which would make it among the wettest Thanksgivings ever in the city.

Officials have rules in place preventing balloons from proceeding down city streets when sustained winds are 25 mph or higher, or if gusts top 35 mph. Watch on Deadline.

It has been revealed that mamdani, hobbled by a recent Achilles tear, remarked he will miss Saturday’s parade due to pending surgery and “doctor’s orders.” But while he walked with a limp, the mayor highlighted he hadn’t lost a step mentally. When a reporter asked about the blowing up of the signature balloons, an annual public ritual held on Thanksgiving Eve near the parade route, Mamdani quipped, “It’s the only kind of inflation we support in Fresh York City.”.

Will Coss, an executive producer and VP at Macy’s who oversees the retailer’s events, stated there will not be a second chance to watch the night-before inflation of the balloons due to the complex logistics of the postponement. He was also asked about the lineup for the event, which could change given that some marching bands (like the one from the University of Albama) are planning to leave town to play at college football games or other events.

Industry observers note that the parade is set to include a number of other special guests and celebrities appearing on floats or performing. An “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will feature performers from fresh and long-running Broadway productions in a special 10-minute medley.

Coss noted it is “an evolving conversation” about potential replacements or planned participants possibly bowing out due to conflicts or travel plans. “We’ve been in communication with all of our participants, from our bands, to our performance groups, to our performing talent. We are optimistic that we’re going to be able to maintain the parade that we set out to produce, and to deliver to Newly introduced York City.”.

It has been revealed that the parade remains a major TV draw, with last year’s pulling in 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, its biggest combined audience on record. By slotting it in on Saturday morning from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET, NBC should be able to have access to a good-sized audience before college football takes over. Still, the viewership patterns on a more conventional Saturday morning versus those on a weekday holiday with preparations for the Thanksgiving feast providing a supply of captive viewers, will be interesting to watch.

In a recent development, in place of the live event, NBC and Peacock will re-air the 2025 edition of the parade on Thursday morning. Mindful of the unusual dynamic in play this year, the network and streamer will double-run the same ads on both Thursday and Saturday to ensure the scale and impact nets out to a satisfying level for buyers.

Recent findings suggest that it is the first time since it began in 1924 that the parade has ever been postponed. In 1971, balloons were grounded by inclement weather but the parade was still held. World War II forced the cancellation of the parade from 1942 to 1944, and the Covid pandemic in 2020 led to organizers converting it into a television-only event around the Herald Square location of Macy’s Department Store.

Industry observers note that this year’s parade is especially significant to Macy’s and NBC, with the latter celebrating its centennial in broadcasting. To help mark the milestone, the parade is set to have 100 of its trademark large balloons.

The importance of NBC’s 100th anniversary is likely to have played a role in the rescheduling. Parent firm NBCUniversal, confirmed early this week that this year’s parade set a revenue record. A windswept and soggy edition of the annual TV fixture would surely have presented myriad production challenges. It possibly would also have left advertisers tuning in to see compromised signage and balloons (some of them branded) swirling precariously around the streets.

“We want to ensure that we’re delivering a parade that’s not only incredible and spectacular, but one also that doesn’t come at the expense of anyone’s safety,” Mamdani noted.

“The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” is wrapping up its eight-episode third season, with the final two episodes now available to stream. The show has certainly made headlines for its enormous budget and ambitious production, with Amazon originally committing to a five-season blueprint and involving the Tolkien Estate in overseeing the adaptation. It’s a fascinating chapter in the franchise’s television history, and thankfully, the story isn’t over yet.

According to recent reports, set five years after the fall of Eregion, the third season finds Middle-earth engulfed in war as Sauron’s (Charlie Vickers) armies continue their march across the land. Watch "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" on Prime Video.

Rather than focusing entirely on his career in the ring, the series also explores the personal, family and cultural pressures that shaped him along the way. This is a more intimate approach to Ali’s story, while the faithful recreation of historic boxing footage also helps bring the story to life. It’s an interesting watch even if you’re not a huge boxing fan.

As he prepares for a career-defining showdown with formidable opponent Sonny Liston (Amin Joseph), the series charts the pivotal moments that helped shape one of boxing’s most recognizable figures.

Watch "The Greatest" on Prime Video.

With romance, comedy and thriller elements in the mix, it’s an interesting option if you're after something a little different.

Sources indicate that the series follows Kang Jae-hee (Seorina), a former special forces operative turned detective who takes on an unusual undercover assignment. While keeping a close eye on her new employer and searching for evidence, Jae-hee finds herself caught up in the family’s complicated affairs. Judge Sides With ABC In First Amendment Lawsuit Against FCC; Puts Halt To Agency’s Early License Renewal Proceeding

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A federal judge has largely sided with ABC in its First Amendment lawsuit claiming that an FCC order to review its broadcast licenses was a retaliatory act by the Trump administration designed to chill its content, whether that be news coverage or jokes from Jimmy Kimmel.
  • District Judge Loren AliKhan issued a preliminary injunction on Wednesday that prohibits the FCC from taking any further action in its license review, concluding that the network was “likely to succeed in their retaliation claim.
  • According to recent reports, “This is not a close case,” she wrote in concluding that the network had shown that the public interest favors court intervention in agency action.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal judge has largely sided with ABC in its First Amendment lawsuit claiming that an FCC order to review its broadcast licenses was a retaliatory act by the Trump administration designed to chill its content, whether that be news coverage or jokes from Jimmy Kimmel.

Recent findings suggest that U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan issued a preliminary injunction on Wednesday that prohibits the FCC from taking any further action in its license review, concluding that the network was “likely to succeed in their retaliation claim.

According to recent reports, “This is not a close case,” she wrote in concluding that the network had shown that the public interest favors court intervention in agency action. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Dancing With The Stars' Finale Recap: Who Takes Home The Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy? Cancellations and Renewals 'Dancing With The Stars: The Next Pro' Renewed For Season 2 At ABC & Prepares To Move Filming To LA.

“No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit,” AliKhan wrote. “But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech.”.

She also rejected the FCC’s effort to dismiss the lawsuit on jurisdictional grounds.

“Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face – loss of their broadcast licenses – the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness,” the judge wrote.

Read the judge’s decision in the ABC case against the FCC.

According to recent reports, in highlighting the urgency of court action, AliKhan cited moves that the network has already taken out of fear of losing their licenses. They include the choice to place James Talarico’s guest appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live on YouTube, outside of the FCC’s authority, as well as ABC’s decision to livestream Trump’s July primetime speech out of fear concern of administration retaliation.

Recent findings suggest that “These alterations to Plaintiffs’ editorial decision making showcase how the Commission’s early license renewal proceedings have already curtailed Plaintiffs’ protected activity,” the judge wrote. “That an objectively reasonable broadcaster faced with the same existential threat would follow suit is beyond debate.”.

The network is the first major media conglomerate to challenge the FCC’s wave of investigations since the start of Donald Trump‘s second term.

ABC filed suit against the FCC in August, claiming that the agency was violating the First Amendment as it ordered the network’s broadcast stations to submit their licenses to an early review.

According to recent reports, the network noted that the agency’s action was unprecedented, creating a chill to its speech and that of other broadcasters given the risk to losing licenses for their eight owned stations. The first of the licenses was not set to expire until 2028.

In claiming regulatory retaliation, the network cited Trump’s attacks on Kimmel and its news coverage, as well as warnings from the president’s FCC Chairman Brendan Carr.

Industry observers note that the judge referenced Trump’s attacks and warnings in her opinion and noted that three of the co-hosts of The View, as well as Kimmel and ABC News reporters have entrires of the White House’s “media offenders” webpage. She said that Trump and Carr’s “call and response” was “no coincidence.”.

She also noted the timing of the FCC’s order for ABC stations to submit to the license review, coming a day after Trump posted on Truth Social that Kimmel should be fired for a skit the previous week.

The FCC has argued that the early license renewal was tied to its inability to obtain documents from the network as part of an investigation of its diversity, equity and inclusion practices. But toward the end of a two-hour hearing last month, the judge asked the agency whether there were other, less drastic alternatives it could have chosen rather than the license review. And in her decision, AliKhan wrote that she did not find the agency’s explanation to be credible.

In a recent development, she wrote, “What is more, Chairman Carr has taken President Trump’s rhetoric as his marching orders. The same week he was tapped to be President Trump’s FCC chair, following months of President Trump’s calling for ‘ABC [to] lose its license’ for how it covered the presidential campaign …. then-Commissioner Carr lauded ‘license revocation’ as a ‘remedy’ to ‘deter this kind of conduct.'”.

During the hearing, Beth Wilkinson, representing the network, compared ABC’s situation to the French Revolution, with people forced on a guillotine, wondering if anything will come down. Losing broadcast licenses, she said, is akin to a “death penalty” for stations.

Sources indicate that the FCC argued that the network had to wait until the review process played out before challenging it, and that the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals, not the district court, is the venue to hear such a case.

But AliKhan concluded that ABC’s First Amendment retaliation claim fell outside the kind of statutory review set up in the Communications Act, directing challenges to the federal appellate court and likely adding months of delay.

Industry observers note that the judge wrote, “To be sure, Plaintiffs would face even greater injury if the FCC ultimately denied their renewal applications. But that does not mean that they are not right now being injured by allegedly being singled out for differential treatment—that is, from facing early license renewal proceedings years in advance of the standard expiration dates as a cudgel to stamp out unfavorable content about President Trump.”.

Carr has initiated investigations and reviews of all of the major broadcast networks. Among other things, he launched a probe of The View earlier this year and whether it had to comply with the agency’s Equal Time Rule.

In a recent development, the judge’s decision was limited to the license renewal proceeding. She also denied ABC’s request for a broader injunction that would prohibit any FCC actions “to coerce or threaten” ABC with sanctions as a way to influence their content. AliKhan wrote that such an injunction could not be issued to something “merely feared.”.

An ABC News spokesperson remarked, “Today’s decision is an vital victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration.”.

A spokesperson for the FCC stated in a statement, “While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law—as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear. The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations.”.

Sources indicate that anna Gomez, the sole Democrat on the FCC, noted in a statement, “For nearly two years, the agency has weaponized its licensing authority to retaliate against broadcasters for exercising their right to free expression, and now a federal court has stepped in to put a check on that conduct. That brings badly needed accountability to a Commission and an administration that have politicized the machinery of government in a sustained campaign of censorship and control.”.

The case had been closely watched by First Amendment advocates and journalism groups.

Bruce Brown, the president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, called the decision “a substantial win not only for ABC, but for all broadcasters.”.

He remarked, “As the court recognized, this is ‘not a close case.’ But it is also a novel case forced on ABC because of the administration’s punitive actions and therefore all the more vital that the federal judiciary stepped in to vindicate First Amendment rights.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple's latest flagship smartwatch, the Apple Watch Series 12, is worth the upgrade. With this model, Apple has upgraded the processor, added a new heart rate sensor, and improved the display durability. It's certainly one of Apple's best smartwatches, but that also means it isn't cheap: All these new features give the new Series 12 a starting price of $399, which only increases if you choose a model with cellular data. However, for Black Friday, you can take up to $100 off the Series 12, bringing the starting price down to $299.

Industry observers note that the three biggest hardware upgrades with the Apple Watch Series 12 are the heart rate sensor, the S11 chip, and Ceramic Shield 2. That heart rate sensor now checks your pulse every five seconds, or 20 times a minute. Apple states the Series 12 checks your heart rate variability 24 times more than the Series 11, and your background heart rate 60 times more frequently than the Series 11. The organization is even so bold as to say the Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate monitor on a wearable.

Powering the new heart rate monitor is the S11 chip, Apple's latest processor for the Apple Watch. The S11 isn't only responsible for these new heart rate features, however. In addition to running the same watchOS 27 features as other compatible Apple Watches, the S11 on the Series 12 can run Audio Intelligence, Apple's new suite of AI-powered audio features. That includes "Live Rewind," which lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation, and "Siri Recaps," which displays summaries of your conversations throughout the day. Finally, the other major advantage with the Series 12 is Ceramic Shield 2. This is a display upgrade that Apple typically reserves for more premium Apple Watch finishes, but this year, the aluminum Series 12 gets it as well. That means the watch should be more durable against scratches and cracks, without you having to upgrade to the more expensive model.

It has been revealed that how much you'll save on a Series 12 depends on the size, color, and model. At this time, Amazon is selling certain colors of the 42mm Series 12 for $299, while certain colors of the 46mm option run $449 (also marked down by $100). You can also save on the cellular models as well: The 42mm option is presently $429 (down from $499), while the 46mm model is $449 (down from $549).

According to recent reports, yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eight years ago, I bought my first Philips Hue product: the Hue Go Portable Lamp.
  • Philips Hue is one of the few tech ecosystems I’ve genuinely enjoyed investing in, and one that has become more valuable to me over time.
  • Ahead of the shopping holiday, I asked Marco Merolla, Executive Vice President and Business Leader of Connected Lighting at Philips Hue, about the company's approach to affordability, product longevity and the future of smart lighting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eight years ago, I bought my first Philips Hue product: the Hue Go Portable Lamp. Eight years later, the bowl-shaped, battery-powered lamp still works, and it has quite a few friends.

Philips Hue is one of the few tech ecosystems I’ve genuinely enjoyed investing in, and one that has become more valuable to me over time. But Philips Hue does have a reputation for being expensive. That's why I consider Black Friday deals one of the best opportunities to either get started with Hue or expand an existing setup.

Ahead of the shopping holiday, I asked Marco Merolla, Executive Vice President and Business Leader of Connected Lighting at Philips Hue, about the company's approach to affordability, product longevity and the future of smart lighting.

His answers shed some light on why customers like me keep coming back, and where there's still room for improvement when it comes to connected smart homes.

In a recent development, I'm vehemently anti-massive-light. One of my proudest domestic achievements is successfully converting my fiancé to the cause, too.

My apartment is laden with lamps, most of which are from IKEA. I also have a Hue light strip running along the back of my Lovesac couch and Hue bulbs in the built-in pendant lights above my kitchen island. But generally, rather than buying smart-specific fixtures, I prefer picking out lamps that complement my mid-century modern decor and making them smart myself.

Merolla described smart lighting as a gradual progression rather than an all-at-once overhaul. Most people start with a single room or routine and build outward as they see how it fits their space. Still, I was curious how Hue reconciles its need to keep selling products with customers' expectations that their relatively expensive lights will last.

If you're just getting started with Philips Hue, this four-pack is an affordable way to turn the lamps you already own into smart lights, complete with adjustable white lighting, millions of colors and the option to expand your setup down the road.

“Our goal is not to encourage replacement for its own sake, but to give consumers meaningful reasons to expand and enhance their existing smart lighting setup as their needs change,” Merolla remarked.

Sources indicate that the other side of that equation is lowering the barrier to entry without fragmenting the system. Hue's more affordable Essential range runs on the same underlying software and ecosystem connectivity as its flagship lights, trimming peak brightness and color performance to hit a friendlier price. It’s a smart option if you're outfitting an entire apartment and don't need top-tier output in every corner lamp..

I've extensively tested competing smart lighting products in varying price ranges from Govee, Wyze and Nanoleaf. Govee, in particular, makes some incredibly fun lighting fixtures, and its adoption of Matter has made it a more compelling option for Apple Home customers like myself.

Industry observers note that but I've experienced software glitches with these other brands over the years. Nearly a decade into my smart home journey, I simply don’t have patience for connected gadgets that don't work as expected 100% of the time. Sharing a home with someone less interested in technology makes reliability and simplicity even more crucial.

“Physical controls remain vital, since not everyone wants to reach for their phone every time they adjust the lights,” Merolla said.

While you don't technically need a Bridge to get started with Hue, I'd recommend picking one up while it's on sale to unlock whole-home lighting control, advanced automations, Apple Home integration and more opportunities to expand your setup.

Despite my investment in Hue, I rarely need to open the app for everyday lighting controls. Between wall-mounted Hue dimmer switches and shortcuts I've configured in my iPhone's Control Center through Apple Home, the lights feel as immediate as traditional switches.

It has been revealed that you don't actually need a Bridge to get started. Bluetooth-enabled Hue bulbs work directly with your phone for up to 10 lights. But upgrading to a Bridge unlocks remote access, advanced automations, Apple Home integration and entertainment synchronization, while scaling up to 50 lights and 12 accessories on the standard model.

If you're eyeing the newer Bridge Pro, you get triple the capacity, wireless placement without an Ethernet tether, and MotionAware, a feature that uses subtle signal shifts across your existing bulbs to detect movement without dedicated motion sensors.

If you're serious about building out your smart home, the Bridge Pro offers more room to expand, faster performance and MotionAware technology that can turn compatible Hue lights into motion sensors.

“The Hue Bridge continues to play an notable role in delivering a robust, connected lighting experience, while innovations such as MotionAware demonstrate how lighting infrastructure can become more intelligent and responsive to people’s needs,” Merolla noted.

If you're planning to expand beyond a few bulbs, I'd invest in the infrastructure now rather than revisit your setup later.

If you've already established a Hue ecosystem, the Philips Hue Play HDMI Sync Box is easily one of my favorite ways to get more out of it.

What I love about the experience is that it isn't limited to a light strip behind my TV. The lights I've already accumulated around my living space can react to what's happening on screen, making my apartment feel like one cohesive entertainment setup.

One of my absolute favorite smart home accessories, the 8K Sync Box lets you synchronize up to 10 compatible Philips Hue lights with what's happening on your TV through connected HDMI devices, making your entire living room feel like an extension of the screen.

Industry observers note that hue has also been finding fresh ways to make entertainment lighting more interesting. Earlier this year, it introduced Sports Live, which uses live soccer match data to trigger lighting effects. It doesn't even require a Sync Box if you already have a Bridge and compatible color lights.

The Sync Box is admittedly a luxury, and it wouldn't be my first Hue purchase if I were starting from scratch. But it's exactly the kind of accessory I'd wait until Black Friday to buy.

It has been revealed that as much as I appreciate Hue's reliability, I'd love to see more intelligence built into the experience. Whenever I add another lamp to my living room, for example, I have to revisit my entertainment area's lighting configuration. Smarter spatial mapping could make that process considerably easier.

The product that started my Philips Hue obsession eight years ago, this compact, bowl-shaped, battery-powered lamp is incredibly versatile for everything from setting the mood at dinner to adding a colorful accent to a bookshelf, and remains one of my favorite entry points into the Hue ecosystem.

In a recent development, I'm not the only one looking for refinements. In a 2026 wishlist discussion on the Philips Hue subreddit, consumers called for more granular brightness controls, better Natural Light scene integration with third-party platforms and the ability to group multiple bulbs in a single fixture.

Merolla told me that the organization sees an opportunity to move beyond simply controlling individual devices.

“We believe the future of smart lighting is less about controlling individual devices and more about creating experiences that naturally respond to the way people live.”.

If I had to rebuild my smart home tomorrow, I'd probably start exactly where I did eight years ago: with a little Hue Go or a handful of smart bulbs.

Recent findings suggest that the beauty of building a smart lighting ecosystem is that you don't need to buy everything at once. And with Black Friday discounts, you can take that first step (or if you’re like me, your next one) for considerably less.

If You Loved 'The Good Daughter,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable.
  • Dark Places has seriously buried secrets.
  • It has been revealed that like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable. The performances, for one—Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy are terrific as estranged sisters Sam and Charlotte Quinn. But it’s also a great story, tracing the corrosive effect of a years-ago trauma on the women and their lawyer father (Brendan Gleeson) amid the slow revelation of many extremely dark secrets. If you want more of that flavor of trauma-driven drama with a tight focus on family bonds, there’s one movie you should watch: 2015's Dark Places.

You want buried secrets? Dark Places has seriously buried secrets. Adapted from the Gillian Flynn novel, the film follows Libby Day (Charlize Theron), who survived the mass murder of her family in 1985. The crime is blamed on her brother Ben, a moody loner whose conviction was based in large part on Libby’s own testimony. For a long time, Libby is financially sustained by donations from people who sympathize with her plight, but three decades after the murders, the money has dried up, and Libby is desperate—so desperate, she agrees to help out a “true crime” club that believes her brother is innocent and is working toward his release.

It has been revealed that like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence. Libby and Ben’s experience mirrors Sam and Charlie’s in many ways, including in the way both Libby and Ben carry secrets for years after the terrible events that took family from them. The stories are also both compelling mysteries, slowly revealing the shocking truths behind one horrific night, and ultimately allowing the characters to better understand one another.

Dark Places also explores the insular, suffocating nature of small-town life, and how rumor and gossip become a poisonous presence in people’s lives. Libby, Ben, Sam, and Charlie all have to deal with others' assumptions and revelations that they've been betrayed by those closest to them, leading to powerful resolutions. If you loved The Good Daughter, you’ll love this movie. Stream Dark Places on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that want more stories about family dynamics around secrets, violence, and explosive emotional confrontations? Here are a few more movies fans of The Good Daughter are bound to enjoy.

There’s no violent crime at the heart of this slow-burn drama—just an explosive chaos agent named Kym, played by Anne Hathaway. If your favorite aspect of The Good Daughter was the relationship between sisters Sam and Charlie, then this movie is perfect. Released from rehab to attend her sister’s wedding, Kym is self-hating, angry, and haunted by a terrible event from her childhood. Her sister, Rachel (Rosemary DeWitt), is welcoming, but has never truly forgiven Kym, and the simmering tension between the sisters and the rest of the family drives a drama that you won’t be able to look away from. Stream Rachel Getting Married on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If you really vibed on the Southern setting, the slow-burn mystery, and the exploration of flawed justice in the modern age depicted in The Good Daughter, check out Where the Crawdads Sing. It’s a slower, dreamier rumination on rural life, violence and its cost, and small-town justice, but it hits the same sweet spot in its story about a woman named Kya (Daisy Edgar-Jones) who was raised in an isolated house in the swamps of North Carolina. Accused in 1969 of a murder, Kya’s story stretches back to her childhood, when she’s slowly abandoned by her entire family, leaving her at age seven to survive on her own. Ostracized as the “swamp girl” by the town, Kya fights to live her life and be loved while facing the unwanted—and violently persistent—attention of the murder victim. It’s about broken families, deeply buried secrets, and what we do to survive. Stream Where the Crawdads Sing on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

The Good Daughter is about life in a small, Southern town, family trauma, and the legal system—which makes A Time to Kill the perfect movie to watch when you finish the show. When a Black man’s daughter is sexually assaulted in Mississippi and her attackers—local members of the Ku Klux Klan—look likely to go free, he violently and publicly murders them. Local lawyer Jake Brigance (Matthew McConaughey) takes on the case, assisted by law student Ellen Roark (Sandra Bullock). They face violent opposition, withering racism, and an unfair legal system that echoes the environment in The Good Daughter in ways fans will appreciate. Stream A Time to Kill on YoutTube or rent it on Prime Video.

The Dry might be as close as you can get to The Good Daughter in terms of tone and story. Although set in Australia instead of the American South, The Dry is a story driven by past crimes and buried secrets in a rural setting just like the show. Twenty years ago, Federal agent Aaron Falk (Eric Bana) fled his hometown when he was suspected of the murder of his girlfriend. When his childhood friend, Luke, appears to have murdered his wife and young son before killing himself, he returns to investigate. The slow revelation of two mysteries—one in the past and one simmering in the drought-stricken present—makes this an ideal companion film to the show. Stream The Dry on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Set in Boston instead of the South, and focused on male friendships instead of a sisters’ bond, Mystic River nevertheless nails the same atmosphere of dread as The Good Daughter. In 1975, boyhood friends Jimmy, Dave, and Sean are traumatized when Dave is abducted and assaulted by two men. In 1990, the three men remain connected in their Boston neighborhood—Jimmy (Sean Penn) is an ex-convict still connected to local crime, Sean (Kevin Bacon) is a State Police detective, and Dave (Tim Robbins) is a blue-collar worker still haunted by his experience. When Jimmy’s daughter is found murdered and Dave seems implicated, Sean and Jimmy launch investigations from either side of the law, with Dave’s fate hanging in the balance. The ending is powerfully brutal, but this story of secrets and suspicion will resonate with fans of the show. Rent Mystic River on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scroll through Amazon for five minutes and you’ll find dozens of $10–20 cases that look, through a thumbnail, almost identical to $50+ aramid fiber ones. Same dark weave, same slim profile, same pitch.

Recent findings suggest that once you actually snap one onto a phone, the differences are obvious. You handle your phone for hours every day, so rough seams around the charging port, awkward cutouts, low-quality materials will make you regret your purchase instantly. With PITAKA’s Black Friday sale taking up to 30% off selected cases, it’s worth breaking down what actually separates a real aramid case from a cheap lookalike, why you should spent the extra money on PITAKA’s high-quality cases.

This post is sponsored by PITAKA.

It has been revealed that plenty of budget cases get the woven look by printing a pattern onto plain plastic. If you’re looking for that style, go for it, but it won’t behave like woven aramid fiber, which lets a case stay rigid and thin without adding much weight.

In a recent development, even genuine aramid cases aren’t all made the same way. The weave, resin, thickness, and surface finish all change how a case feels in use. PITAKA uses woven aramid fiber in two main weights: 600D and 1500D. Those numbers measure yarn density; the finer 600D weave feels a bit smoother and produces a slightly thinner shell than 1500D. Whatever case you choose, look past the word “premium” and check whether the maker actually spells out what the case is made of.

Recent findings suggest that most aramid cases stick to plain black and gray. PITAKA’s Fusion Weaving method blends colored fibers and multiple weave styles directly into the shell instead of printing a graphic on the outside. PITAKA indicates the process requires tight control over fabric tension and how fibers cross between layers. In practice, it means you can pick something colorful like the Sunset colorway without giving up the feel of woven fiber, or stick with classic Black & Grey if you prefer a quieter look.

Online listings spend almost all their time showing off the back of a case, even though your fingers spend just as much time on the sides, buttons, and bottom edge. An awkward camera cutout makes quick shots annoying, a tight port opening fights bulkier charging cables, and sharp edges dig into your hand on a long call.

Rather than selling one shell in ten colors, PITAKA splits its lineup into three builds:.

If you use a magnetic charger, wallet, or grip, how the magnets are built into the case matters just as much as the outer material. Sticking a separate magnet ring inside a shell usually adds extra layers and thickness.

PITAKA’s Amber Magnet Film process bonds coated magnets directly with the aramid fiber and resin under heat and pressure. That keeps the magnets enclosed without bulking up the case, which is the kind of detail you won’t spot in a photo but will notice in your pocket.

In a recent development, spending more on a case doesn’t guarantee it’s better, and plenty of $20 cases are completely fine. Genuine aramid fiber by itself doesn’t guarantee better drop protection either. A thin shell like Edge is made for people who hate bulky cases. If drop protection is your main concern, look at a cushioned option like Cairn or Summa, and compare actual edge coverage and model-specific testing instead of judging by price or material alone.

What you’re really paying for with a higher-end aramid case is how it feels and fits every time you pick up your phone.

In a recent development, if you already want a thinner, better-finished case, Black Friday takes some of the sting out of the price. PITAKA’s Amazon offers run November 19–30, with discounts varying by device and colorway:.

Recent findings suggest that buying directly from the PITAKA official website? Code PTKPR12 takes an extra 5% off from November 10 through December 31. It’s separate from the Amazon sale, so double-check eligible products and your final total at checkout.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. Microdrama Revenues Hit $20B, But Profits Outside China Still Weak – MPA Report

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The global microdrama business is booming, but outside of China, where ByteDance rules the roost, profits haven’t yet caught up with revenues.
  • In a recent development, that’s according to a Media Partners Asia (MPA) report, which reveals revenues on a global basis are estimated to rise 24% year-on-year to hit $20B in 2026.
  • The MPA’s second annual Micro-Drama Economy report notes that outside of China, where microdramas first emerged, every 56 cents in a dollar are spent on marketing and another 18 cents goes to app stores and payment providers, which is significantly reducing earnings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The global microdrama business is booming, but outside of China, where ByteDance rules the roost, profits haven’t yet caught up with revenues.

In a recent development, that’s according to a Media Partners Asia (MPA) report, which reveals revenues on a global basis are estimated to rise 24% year-on-year to hit $20B in 2026. That will hit $32B by 2031, a growth rate of 9.8% per year, but profitability is still thin.

The MPA’s second annual Micro-Drama Economy report notes that outside of China, where microdramas first emerged, every 56 cents in a dollar are spent on marketing and another 18 cents goes to app stores and payment providers, which is significantly reducing earnings. Related Stories News Dogwoof Moves Into Microdrama Game With Tattle TV Deal News Women In Vertical Media: Execs From Shorties Studios, aTwist & Eris Join Inaugural Advisory Circle.

In a recent development, excluding China, the microdrama biz is worth $4.87B, with the U.S. the largest at $1.71B, but has fallen 2% year-over-year and will be overtaken by Asia Pacific (excluding China) by 2029. The overall revenue figure will grow to $11B in 2031. Watch on Deadline.

The MPA noted the two biggest microdrama groups take revenues of more than $1B a year, but within that DramaBox recorded a net margin of 3.2% in 2025 and ReelShort lost $12M, though it made an $8M profit the first quarter of this year.

According to recent reports, dramaBox and GoodShort, which confirmed a merger at the end of October, along with ReelShort, Kunlun and NetShort collectively account for 65% of revenues outside of China, where the real action is right now. All four apps are Chinese-owned or backed. India is providing the fastest growth, with revenues tripling this year, as local platforms Kuku TV and Story TV boomed and JioStar debuted in the space in April with JioHotstar service Tadka. India is also the largest Asian market outside China with $322M.

MPA’s assessment is that the microdrama business outside of China is not yet settled on a model, but TikTok is predicted to be a dominant force, as it is “positioned on every side” – selling apps’ advertising, carrying their series and, through its free app PineDrama, competing with them.

TikTok’s parent, ByteDance is applying the model that shaped the Chinese market – using free, advertising-funded apps to gain audiences first and monetizing later – and MPA predicts it will gain “significant scale in both the U.S.” and Southeast Asia by 2031. Of course, ByteDance was forced to sell a majority of its shares in TikTok in the U.S., but does retain a minority stake.

YouTube and Meta are not expected to make a major impression on the microdrama space, while locally the likes of Vigloo in Korea and Fuji TV’s Fod Short in Japan are competing with Chinese-backed apps.

In a recent development, china accounts for 76% of total microdrama revenues ($15.2B), following 90% growth in 2025. This will slow to 6.7% in 2031 as viewing plateaus. The MPA doesn’t estimate profits in China as none of the leading players such as top trio ByteDance, Tencent and Kuaishou single microdrama out in their financial reporting.

According to recent reports, advertising on free services took over paid viewing last year, and this year accounts for 69% of revenues, That will grow to 79% in 2031. ByteDance, which operates Hongguo and Douyin, earning 59% of China’s revenues. ByteDance, Tencent and Kuaishou collectively account for 82% of the market.

MPA calculates revenue as what viewers, advertisers and brands pay before app-store and payment fees; and outside China it covers dedicated apps and their web stores, not general social feeds. In China, MPA’s estimates exclude producers’ spending on AI models and platform investment, which are both included in the National Radio and Television Administration’s RMB100B estimate for 2025.

“Demand for micro drama is established in every major market, but outside China this is still an emerging business, and it has yet to show that it can earn a durable profit,” said Vivek Couto, CEO and Executive Director of MPA.

“The leading apps spend more than half of their revenue to acquire viewers, and most of those viewers do not pay. Consolidation has begun, and China has already moved to free, advertising-funded viewing. The companies that endure will be those that retain their viewers, bill them directly and invest in titles worth returning to.”.

Recent findings suggest that the MPA report raised a further notable asides: fresh title listings on apps outside China rose from about 100,000 in 2025 to 440,000 in 2026, and 75% were made with AI. This counts series that are made in different languages more than once. MPA’s research shows an AI-made title costs “about a tenth of a series filmed in Los Angeles,” it added.

“AI has made a title cheap enough to test almost any idea, and catalogues have filled accordingly,” said Myat Pan Phyu (May), Lead Analyst, Micro Drama and Vertical Video for MPA. “Viewing has moved far less: live action still dominates the leading titles on most of the platforms we track.

“What decides a platform’s economics is how many of its titles earn back the marketing spent on them. That favours companies with established IP, stars and audiences of their own, which is why local broadcasters, studios and telecom operators matter to the next phase.”.

AirTag 2 (now only $18, down from $29) launched earlier this year after a five-year wait, and in my experience there are two big improvements that make it worth the upgrade.

Precision Finding is Apple’s best AirTag feature, letting you get step-by-step, highly precise directions to your lost item. But with the original AirTag, you had to be in fairly close proximity before you could benefit from Precision Finding.

With AirTag 2, Apple added a second-generation Ultra Wideband chip that makes Precision Finding now available from up to 1.5x farther away than before. It’s a huge increase that I’ve definitely noticed.

Industry observers note that this expansion of Precision Finding to greater distances means the feature is now available a lot more often than with the old AirTag. For this reason alone, I highly recommend AirTag 2.

When you’re trying to find a lost item, Precision Finding isn’t the only tool AirTag offers. There’s also a built-in speaker that can play a sound, triggered by your iPhone, to help you track it down.

With AirTag 2, Apple has made the built-in speaker 50% louder than before. The company states this enables hearing it from up to twice as far away.

I’ve been impressed by how loud the AirTag speaker is able to get now. Between the new speaker and upgraded Precision Finding, Apple has made AirTag 2 better in the ways that users are likely to care about most.

You can buy AirTag 2 for $18 on Amazon (regularly $29) for a limited time.

#119855. Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3495 w)
